The vendor has provided the following: The TF-1700 was a hand-built sports car produced by Naylor Bros and later the Hutson Car Company between 1984 and 1992. It was developed as an improved form of the original MG TF with increased power and improved suspension, and braking. The engine used was Austin-Rover's 1.7-litre, O-Series,overhead-camshaft unit. These cars were hand-built in the Bradford factory to a very high standard and even cost more than a Morgan when new! If you have ever driven a 1950's MG TF/TD, then this has all the looks but with a much better drive due to the larger engine, more modern gearbox, and brakes! 100 cars carrying the Naylor badge were produced in 1985/86, and then in 1986, Naylor Cars were acquired by the Hutson Car Company, where a further 61 cars with the Hutson badge were produced. They were fully type-approved and had full backing from the Austin Rover Group. This car (chassis no. SA9TFS1M1MA013161) is number '161', the very last car completed by the factory . Kept on showroom display for several years before being registered for the road in 1997. The car has covered just 27, 900 miles from new and is in good condition, and runs/drives superbly. It has been maintained fastidiously by Yorkshire Restorations and, most recently, has had the following work completed: Early 2023 - Replacement original engine sourced by the Hutson Motor Company installed Early 2023 - Brand new three-part clutch fitted Late 2023 - All hoses replaced and a new radiator remanufactured and fitted February 2024 - Full service, tune up, rebuild of the carb, brake service, along with all oil seals replaced(at a cost of £1,940) May 2024 - New alternative and rod bush fitted in May 2024 (at a cost of £410) May 2024 - 5 brand new tyres fitted and wheels balanced July 2024 - Full service undertaken August 2024 - New rear shock absorbers and springs fitted. There is also a new set of front springs to come with the car, but they are yet to be fitted October 2024 - Rear axle fully rebuilt (at a cost of £1,665) December 2024 - New distributor and rotor arm fitted (at a cost of £275) September 2025 - Exhaust had a new bracket fitted and welded January 2026 - Nearside Front Track rod end ball joint replaced July 2026 – Full service undertaken The car comes complete with two keys (one with the original company keyring!), operation manual, service book and owners wallet, workshop manual (printed and on CD), comprehensive service/ history file (in bespoke Hutson ring binder!), original brochures, Naylor/ Hutson books, car magazines (where the car was road tested), Naylor Car Club magazines and even a matching toy model! A bespoke green indoor car cover (RRP: £145) is also included in the sale, along with a pair of new genuine old stock seatbelts, new front springs (mentioned above), and a wicker basket. The vendor has provided the following: Built between 1952 and 1954, the Austin A40 Somerset was built to be a British family car and was the successor to the earlier Austin A40 Devon. The Somerset featured rounded American-style bodywork, hydraulic brakes (which in this particular car have been upgraded to be servo-assisted - so they actually work), a 4-speed column shift gearbox mated to a 1.2l engine capable of powering the car to a claimed 70MPH (Downhill with the wind behind you, but we definitely don't recommend trying, we've never had her above 50MPH). The car has a lovely original interior, which has not been molested or modified during its life. With tan leather seats, the addition of seat belts, both front and rear, and all of the original Baker light switches and original carpets make for a lovely place to sit. The A40 Somerset was considered the last 'true' Austin as it was the last car released before the company joined with Nuffield to form BMC. This particular car has been well looked after, comes complete with a lot of spares, and a great deal of paperwork. She's been well loved and starts up on the button the first time with no problems and no smoke. The car has always been kept on trickle charge and has been stored in a dry garage for our ownership. The paintwork is not perfect but is very respectable for a car of her age, as the paintwork is largely original, apart from the front right wing, which has clearly been repainted. If you want a mint condition car, this one isn't for you. If you want a genuine, honest, and about as original a car as you can get for this age, and it is in very good condition, she is perfect! We've certainly been happy with her for the last however many years, bringing back memories of when I originally owned one of these cars back when I could still bend my legs and didn't make involuntary noises getting in and out of it, which sadly is the reason for selling her. She just isn't practical at my age anymore. Share this

title: HAND MADE 1/8th SCALE MODEL COVENTRY KNIGHT 47 CARAVAN
description_block: Location: PICKERING You can view from: Wednesday 13 May 2026 - Tuesday 19 May 2026 Please note: We do not ship memorabilia items. Please arrange to collect your items in person. 1/8TH SCALE MODEL - COVENTRY KNIGHT 47 This is a large scratch built model of a 1947 Coventry Knight caravan which I built a few years ago. The real vans were the brainchild of innovative designer Clifford Dawtrey and were built by Coventry Steel Caravans Ltd at The Old Corn Exchange, Warwick. The vans were often utilised as mobile banks etc. The fully fitted luxury caravans cost more than a house in 1947, and few could afford them, so were rare even back then and obviously very scarce today. There was a Coventry Knight Owners Club set up in the 40's, and there is still a loyal following today. I wanted to build a model of one as I have never seen one represented in model form, whether scratch built or even diecast. The model is approximately 1:8 scale, and measures 775mm long (890mm including towbar) x 286mm wide x 355mm tall. The weight is about 9kg. I must stress that the model is definitely not museum standard quality. It is very home-made, and looks it, and the finish can best be described as naively scruffy. It is built from recycled materials and stuff normally thrown away as rubbish. My background is in art rather than engineering and I think that shows, but I hope that I have captured the feel and atmosphere of the real thing. Dimensionally, it is bound to be incorrect in places, because I only had photos to work from and have never been inside one of these caravans. CHASSIS/FLOOR The chassis, such as it is, comprises two wooden longitudinals with a floor of foam board and Corriboard topped with real marble vinyl flooring, which looks the part. The corner steady jacks are meant to raise and lower by means of long M4 screws, and sort of work, but they are admittedly a bit of a bodge and could do with being remade by someone with an engineering bent. The wheels are rather wobbly home made resin fabrications, but they still look better than any proprietary wheels I could buy. The vendor has provided the following: The vendor of this 1993 Honda CBR900RR Fireblade is the Bangers & Cash: Restoring Classics team. They write: We bought this 90’s icon back in Feb 2026. We had been after one for a while, so when K125 HRM came up for auction in relatively good nick, our hand was in the air. Some may say it stayed in the air for a little too long as we did have to part with £4000 in order to secure it, but we told our finance manager that it would all be worth it once they could watch us ride it down the runway back at HQ. The bike was first registered in the Netherlands in 1993 and then brought over to the UK in 2016 where it has been with 3 owners (4 including us!). When we thought about the work required to do on this Blade, there was one crack-team of bike mechanics which came to mind. They’ve completed countless bike restorations for us on the show - at least one from each decade dating back to the 50’s…but we’ve always thought Rob & Bri had a 90’s sports bike itch to scratch, so the bike was sent out towards the Humbar Estuary in East Yorkshire. After their surprisingly warm reception of the bike, Rob & Bri got to work. In their own words, the work completed was: The headlight beam had to be addressed, as it was set for driving on the right side of the road - it soon became apparent that getting UK headlights were prohibitively expensive - so a beam deflector was located and fitted - making the bike fit for MOT… There was a broken front fork shroud, so that was replaced with some internet help The exhaust end-can was untidy, so went to Russ at Platinum paint A yolk protector was located and fitted as keys had marked the top yolk The fairing panels and fuel tank came off, and had a good clean and polish. This also enabled the inner components to be checked and cleaned The bike had sun-bleaching on some panels, so they were brought back to life After a good clean and tidy of wheels etc, the bike went back together Oil and battery checked, the Blade was re-started and the electrics tested Once complete the Honda went for its MOT, which it passed and is valid until June 2026. The bike returned back to the Restos production team, where true to our word we did indeed give it a good test ride on the runway! For context, our HQ is at Leeds East Airport. The finance team weren’t entirely convinced by our display but they are looking forward to seeing the bike take new ownership in July’s auction. PLEASE NOTE: We take great pride in restoring our vehicles but they are classics, they will not be immaculate and they will no doubt need ongoing maintenance and repair. We suggest you make your own checks first. Share this

title: HAND MADE 1/8th SCALE MODEL BEDFORD DUPLE VISTA COACH
description_block: Location: PICKERING Please note: We do not ship memorabilia items. Please arrange to collect your items in person. 1/8th Scale Model - Bedford Duple Vista 25 Coach 1967 (29 seater) This is a totally unique home-made model built using recycled materials and stuff usually thrown away as rubbish. APPROX. DIMENSIONS:- WIDTH= 305mm; HEIGHT= 375mm; LENGTH= 943mm APPROX WEIGHT OF COMPLETE MODEL= 16.3 KG I originally built this model in 1995 but have recently rebuilt the bodywork and made a new chassis/floor from scrap wood and plywood. Although the wheels do revolve, I would describe it as a static model. The real vehicle on which the model is based is a Bedford VAS5 Duple Vista 25 C29F, body number 1211/53, built in 1967. It was new to Fale of Combe Down then acquired second hand by Adkins Coaches of Upper Boddington via dealer Erringtons of Evington. Adkins operated the vehicle from 1974 to 1989 when it was withdrawn from service and stored. David Adkins very kindly allowed me to take extensive measurements of the coach. Sadly, we are now at a point where very few 1960's Duple coaches are still extant. Most of the body types now only have two or three examples still in existence and the Vista 25 is no exception. However, thankfully the model was immortalised by Corgi as a diecast toy, so building this very large version has been a labour of love. It has taken a thousand hours of work and at least a gallon of adhesive, but I hope the end result is worth it. A change of circumstances is the reason I am selling it. The chassis is not accurate or detailed at all, just the top of the engine is superficially modelled because it shows when the internal engine cover is removed. The simple wooden chassis comprises 2 longitudinals with a plywood floor on top. The wheels are fabricated from glass fibre, filler and milliput. The front wheels are poseable to a degree. The wheel arches are fabricated using steel from old biscuit tins. The bodywork is however much more fully detailed, but my background is in art rather than engineering, so must stress this is not a museum standard Share this
